title: Treaty of Westphalia (1648)
key_facts: Series of peace treaties signed in Münster and Osnabrück ending the Thirty Years’ War
Recognized state sovereignty and non‑intervention within the Holy Roman Empire
Reconfigured religious settlements (cuius regio, eius religio extended to Calvinists)
causes: Prolonged devastation and stalemate in the Thirty Years’ War
Diplomatic pressure among European powers to stabilize Central Europe
Need to codify new political-religious balance
outcome: Ended the Thirty Years’ War in the Empire and Eighty Years’ War between Spain and the Dutch Republic
Affirmed territorial sovereignty of princes and non‑interference principles
Marked a shift toward modern interstate diplomacy
impacts: Foundation for concepts of sovereignty and the modern international system
Religious pluralism formalized within the Empire
Diminished Habsburg universalist claims; rise of France and Sweden
